Families across Papua New Guinea’s Highlands are facing depleted harvests and the threat of hunger after the El Niño weather pattern brought frost and prolonged dry conditions that have destroyed food gardens providing sustenance and income for thousands of households.

The five-minute advert for a multipurpose disinfectant, released across many online platforms at the end of May, features a man comparing his girlfriend with his former partner.

rfi.title: Fear of mines alone could disrupt Strait of Hormuz shipping, warns French admiral
rfi.description: The Strait of Hormuz has reopened under a fragile United States-Iran deal, but it remains under close watch after maritime authorities warned of suspected and confirmed mines in the area. Former French Navy Admiral Éric Lavault – who headed France's mine warfare and seabed operations, and commanded the navy's bomb-disposal divers – told RFI that even without proof the strait has been mined, it must be checked before commercial shipping can return to normal.

rfi.title: Paris court gives oil giant TotalEnergies deadline to tighten climate policies
rfi.description: A court in Paris ruled on Thursday that energy giant TotalEnergies must account for its consumers’ greenhouse gas emissions, giving the French company six months to adjust a legally mandated risk assessment.

rfi.title: France told to do more to protect children from human trafficking
rfi.description: France must step up efforts to prevent human trafficking and improve support for victims, particularly children and young people, the Council of Europe has said, warning that weaknesses in the country's child protection system continue to leave minors exposed to exploitation.

rfi.title: Relief in sight as temperatures set to fall in France after record heatwave
rfi.description: Temperatures are expected to fall in France from Thursday evening after another day of extreme heat that put 72 of mainland France's 96 departments on red alert, affecting more than 50 million people.

rfi.title: South African anti-migrant groups defend planned ‘Liberation March’
rfi.description: A coalition of South African organisations campaigning against undocumented migrants has defended its plans for nationwide demonstrations on 30 June, insisting the marches will be peaceful despite rising tensions and recent deadly unrest.

rfi.description: Kenyan police put on a massive show of force Thursday in a bid to prevent protests marking two years since a landmark Gen Z uprising.

rfi.title: Macron to host Meloni in Antibes as France and Italy seek closer ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the French seaside resort of Antibes, as the two leaders try to revive a relationship that has been marked by political differences.

rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will not attend a major conference on rebuilding Ukraine being held in Poland this week, as a dispute between the two countries over Second World War remembrance threatens to overshadow talks.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Thapelo Maseko scored mid way through the second half against South Korea to take South Africa into the knockout stages at a World Cup for the first time.

rfi.title: Digital euro wins key EU backing as lawmakers approve draft rules
rfi.description: The European Union has moved a step closer to creating a digital euro, after members of the European Parliament passed a crucial vote on the virtual currency.

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

rfi.title: France announces first Ebola case in doctor returned from DR Congo
rfi.description: French health authorities on Wednesday announced the first confirmed case of Ebola identified on national territory – a doctor who had returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

rfi.title: Switzerland outwit Canada to claim Group B at 2026 World Cup
rfi.description: Switzerland claimed top spot in Group B at the World Cup on Wednesday following a 2-1 win over Canada in Vancouver.

rfi.title: Seven European countries urge ‘immediate halt’ to Sudan violence
rfi.description: Seven European countries have called on Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to immediately stop their assault on El-Obeid, a city in Sudan's North Kordofan state, warning of credible signs that a major offensive could be imminent as civilians face worsening shortages of food, water and fuel.

rfi.title: Portugal delays handover of French mother accused of abandoning children
rfi.description: Portuguese authorities have refused to immediately extradite to France a 41-year-old woman suspected of abandoning her two young children, who were found last month crying at the side of a road south of Lisbon.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch was inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday in a sombre ceremony, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the country’s most symbolic events.

rfi.title: French government begins disciplinary action over child abuse case failings
rfi.description: The French government has announced disciplinary action against a magistrate and two gendarmerie officers over the handling of a suspect in child abuse case, which has lead to public outcry. This comes on the heels of a report which pointed to serious failings of the justice system, particularly with regards to minors.

euronews.title: European trade unions call for World Cup-style ‘cooling breaks’ for workers as temperatures soar
euronews.description: The European Trade Union Confederation is pressing the European Commission to set a maximum working temperature law, warning that extreme heat now poses a predictable and preventable threat to workers across the continent.

euronews.description: The European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) has presented a proposal for European legislation to protect workers' health during heatwaves.

euronews.title: Parisians sleep in parks to cool down during heatwave
euronews.description: Some Parisians are spending the night in city parks to escape sweltering apartments as an intense heatwave continues across France.

euronews.description: Rutte pushed back gently against Trump's latest NATO complaints, saying, “I know there have been isolated cases about which you are really disappointed, but generally speaking, your European allies have been there with you."

euronews.description: New images from La Guaira on 25 June revealed widespread destruction after twin earthquakes struck Venezuela's Caribbean coast, damaging buildings, roads and key public infrastructure.

euronews.title: Brussels tightens rules on US cloud providers as it pushes for tech sovereignty
euronews.description: The European Commission has decided that Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services should face strict rules to improve cloud competition. The move risks angering Washington as Brussels pushes the European tech sovereignty agenda.

euronews.description: Production on Bond 26 is set to begin next year. The expectation is that the official announcement for the next 007 actor will happen by the end of 2026.

euronews.description: The French navy boarded a tanker suspected of belonging to Russia's so-called "ghost fleet" in the Mediterranean, the fifth such operation since September 2025, as Paris steps up efforts to enforce sanctions linked to the war in Ukraine.

euronews.title: Leonard Cohen estate slams use of 'Hallelujah' at Trump's Freedom 250 rally
euronews.description: Donald Trump had announced earlier in June that 'Hallelujah' would be performed at the opening of the Great American State Fair, fuelling the long-term feud between the US president and the estate of Leonard Cohen.

euronews.title: Central Asia’s first Paragliding World Cup is taking place in Kazakhstan
euronews.description: Kazakhstan’s Zhetysu region is hosting the first Paragliding World Cup in Central Asia, bringing together around 150 pilots from 33 countries. The main discipline of the World Cup is cross-country flying.

euronews.title: IRGC warns ships off Oman's corridor in Hormuz as Rubio draws line on tolls
euronews.description: The IRGC warned that any vessel navigating outside Tehran's designated routes was acting illegally, directly rejecting Oman's newly announced temporary corridor, as Rubio told a GCC meeting the US would not accept fees regardless of how they are framed.

euronews.title: How much do we really know about microplastics? | Euronews Tech Talks
euronews.description: Microplastics pollute our planet, raising questions about their impact on human health and the environment. This Q&A episode of Euronews Tech Talks sums up what science knows, and does not know, about them.

euronews.title: International community pledges aid to Venezuela after devastating earthquakes
euronews.description: The United States Geological Survey has estimated that the final death toll could be between 10,000 and 100,000 people.

euronews.title: Bigger than Jupiter, lighter than cotton candy: Astronomers discover two ‘super-puff’ planets
euronews.description: The two planets orbiting a star 1,110 light-years away are the biggest exoplanets ever found with a density lower than cotton candy, and may be mostly made of hydrogen and helium.

euronews.title: Europe summer travel trends: Short breaks, family holidays and coolcations drive demand
euronews.description: From quick getaways to heatwave-avoiding escapes, new data from Trip.com reveals the trends that are shaping summer travel across Europe in 2026.

lemonde.title: Pendant la canicule, les parents d’élèves indignés par « l’absence de cadre » pour les écoles : « On a dû s’organiser en catastrophe »
lemonde.description: Les conditions d’accueil des enfants en classe se dégradent et les parents tentent de s’adapter, entre télétravail, jours de congé ou relais auprès d’autres adultes. Tous déplorent l’impréparation des pouvoirs publics et craignent les années à venir.

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : au moins 164 morts et près de 1 000 blessés, selon un nouveau bilan provisoire
lemonde.description: Deux tremblements de terre, dont l’un devenu le plus puissant en plus d’un siècle dans le pays, ont frappé l’ouest de Caracas, dans la soirée de mercredi. Les spécialistes redoutent un bilan « lourd » et des dégâts « importants ».

lemonde.title: Procès climatique contre TotalEnergies : la justice ordonne au groupe pétrolier de prendre en compte les émissions de CO₂ de ses clients
lemonde.description: Depuis 2020, une coalition d’associations et la Ville de Paris demandent à la justice de contraindre la multinationale à réduire ses émissions de gaz à effet de serre. Le tribunal vient d’exiger que le géant pétrogazier intègre dans son plan de vigilance les émissions de ses clients. Une avancée significative.

lemonde.title: LFI s’indigne après la diffusion d’un montage audio « fallacieux » mettant en cause Jean-Luc Mélenchon ; France Culture présente ses excuses
lemonde.description: Au cours d’un entretien avec Marine Le Pen, le présentateur de la matinale, Guillaume Erner, avait repris un montage trouvé sur les réseaux sociaux. Le parti de Jean-Luc Mélenchon a annoncé avoir saisi l’Arcom.

lemonde.title: En Côte d’Ivoire, les liens secrets du défunt président Henri Konan Bédié avec le groupe français Castel, géant de la bière en Afrique
lemonde.description: L’ex-chef de l’Etat ivoirien, personnage politique central du pays, a détenu, par l’intermédiaire de sociétés offshore, des parts dans la Solibra, leader ivoirien des boissons alcoolisées, et filiale du groupe Castel, ainsi qu’une enquête du « Monde » le documente pour la première fois.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : à New York, le football envahit la ville où le basket est roi
lemonde.description: Le Mondial nord-américain pourrait permettre au ballon rond de trouver toute sa place à New York. Les terrains de « soccer » se multiplient dans la ville, et les pratiquants, toujours plus nombreux, commencent à faire de l’ombre aux sports américains traditionnels.

lemonde.title: La bataille des économistes Philippe Aghion et Paul Krugman sur le décrochage de l’Europe
lemonde.description: Philippe Aghion, « Prix Nobel d’économie » 2025, constate un décrochage inquiétant de la productivité européenne comparée à celle des Etats-Unis tandis que Paul Krugman, « Prix Nobel d’économie » 2008, souligne le maintien de la prospérité du Vieux Continent. Serait-il possible qu’ils aient tous les deux raison ?, s’interroge Pascal Riché, journaliste au « Monde », dans sa chronique.

lemonde.title: Roundup : la Cour suprême des Etats-Unis donne raison à Bayer face aux milliers de plaintes pour risque de cancer
lemonde.description: Le géant allemand s’est félicité de la décision en faveur de son herbicide, à base de glyphosate, accusé d’être cancérigène et à l’origine de procès coûtant plus de 10 milliards de dollars au groupe.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les dernières informations
lemonde.description: La marine française a arraisonné un pétrolier soupçonné de faire partie de la flotte fantôme russe. Il s’agit du cinquième arraisonnement de ce type depuis septembre 2025 de la part de la France.

lemonde.title: Le gendarme du renseignement sur la retenue face à la question de l’« entrisme » islamiste
lemonde.description: La Commission nationale de contrôle des techniques de renseignement a présenté, mercredi, son rapport annuel. Vincent Mazauric, son président, a rappelé que le législateur n’a pas prévu l’utilisation des techniques de renseignement pour lutter contre « l’entrisme » islamiste, alors qu’un projet de loi sur cette question est en préparation.

lemonde.title: Gérard Brémond, fondateur du groupe touristique Pierre & Vacances, est mort à l’âge de 88 ans
lemonde.description: Gérard Brémond avait conçu la station de ski Avoriaz et imaginé un nouveau modèle de résidences, où des particuliers achètent à prix réduits des appartements confiés ensuite en location à Pierre & Vacances, qui réserve à ces propriétaires un droit de séjour.

lemonde.title: Pétrole : les cours renouent avec leurs niveaux d’avant la guerre au Moyen-Orient
lemonde.description: La détente des prix traduit l’afflux des cargaisons en provenance du golfe Arabo-Persique, avec la reprise du trafic dans le détroit d’Ormuz.

lemonde.title: Les meilleurs vins rosés de 2026 : la sélection du « Monde »
lemonde.description: Rémi Barroux, Stéphane Davet, Laure Gasparotto et Sébastien Jenvrin ont goûté plus de 300 rosés de toutes régions, pour en sélectionner 72. Avec 29 vins, la Provence tient le haut du pavé, et 70 % des cuvées sont en bio ou en biodynamie.

lemonde.title: « François d’Assise, la sainteté est un sport de combat », sur France Culture : une « Grande Traversée » pour dévoiler l’homme derrière le saint
lemonde.description: L’enquête en cinq volets de Céline Laurens rappelle que, avant de devenir l’une des figures majeures du christianisme, il fut un jeune homme en rupture avec son milieu et son époque.

lemonde.title: Guadeloupe : les élus réunis en congrès demandent à l’Etat de prendre en charge la refonte du réseau d’eau
lemonde.description: Lors du Congrès de l’eau, organisé par le conseil départemental de Guadeloupe, les élus ont unanimement demandé à l’Etat la mise en place d’une opération d’intérêt national pour la refonte des infrastructures d’eau potable et d’assainissement, vétustes depuis des années.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : les mêmes valeurs mais pas la même méthode, un électorat de gauche partagé à un an du scrutin
lemonde.description: A partir de l’enquête électorale d’Ipsos, réalisée en avril auprès de 11 000 personnes, la Fondation Jean Jaurès propose une radiographie des électeurs de gauche, qui partagent un même projet de société mais divergent sur les moyens d’y parvenir.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi les séismes qui ont frappé le Venezuela sont aussi inhabituels et dévastateurs
france24fr.description: La principale hypothèse retenue après le choc sismique qui a frappé le Venezuela, dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi, est la survenue d’un phénomène relativement rare : la succession très rapide et proche de deux secousses majeures “jumelles”.

france24fr.title: La justice ordonne à TotalEnergies de prendre en compte les émissions carbone de ses clients
france24fr.description: Le tribunal judiciaire de Paris s’est prononcé jeudi dans l'affaire dite du devoir de vigilance de TotalEnergies. Dans sa décision, il a enjoint au groupe pétrolier de compléter son plan de vigilance dans un délai de ​six mois pour y inclure les émissions indirectes liées à ses produits.

france24fr.title: Au Bénin, des créateurs misent sur les jeux pour faire découvrir le patrimoine
france24fr.description: Au Bénin, des créateurs misent sur les jeux vidéo et les expériences interactives pour valoriser le patrimoine culturel. Cartes à collectionner, réalité augmentée et univers immersifs inspirés du gaming deviennent ainsi de nouveaux moyens de faire découvrir l’histoire et les traditions aux plus jeunes.

france24fr.title: Canicule : le corps humain mis à rude épreuve
france24fr.description: La France connaît des épisodes de chaleur inhabituels qui mettent les organismes à rude épreuve, au moment de l’exposition mais aussi dans les heures qui suivent. Contrairement aux populations vivant dans des pays régulièrement confrontés à de fortes températures, nos modes de vie, nos infrastructures et nos habitudes ne sont pas encore pleinement adaptés à ce type de conditions, une situation qui pourrait toutefois évoluer si ces épisodes se multiplient. france24fr.title: En France, 'on vit une crise démocratique profonde et on sent qu'on est à la croisée des chemins'
france24fr.description: Le Chef de la rubrique politique-société chez The Conversation, David Bornstein nous rejoint pour Derrière l'Image. Six ans après la photographie symbolique des 150 citoyens de la Convention citoyenne pour le climat réunis à l'Élysée, le constat dressé dans cet entretien est celui d'un décalage croissant entre l'ambition affichée de renouveler la démocratie française et les résultats effectivement obtenus.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Israël conditionne de nouveau son retrait du Liban au désarmement du Hezbollah
Canicule: une catastrophe agricole
france24fr.description: Les canicules sont les plus redoutées des catastrophes climatiques par les agriculteurs. Contre la sécheresse soudaine et les fortes chaleurs qui cuisent les cultures, pas grand chose à faire. Les pertes de rendements sont inévitables. L'adaptation de l'agriculture doit se faire sur le long terme, en sélectionnant des semences et en adaptant la configuration des champs. Mais même ces techniques ont leurs limites face à un réchauffement climatique qui continuerait de s'amplifier.

france24fr.title: Conférence sur l'Ukraine : après les tensions, Kiev et Varsovie jouent l'apaisement
france24fr.description: Alors que s'est ouverte, jeudi, la 5e conférence sur la reconstruction en Ukraine, les responsables politiques ukrainiens et polonais ont ouvert l'événement en affichant leur proximité retrouvée, alors que fin mai les relations s'étaient refroidies entre les deux pays voisins.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : plus gros séismes depuis 126 ans, l'aide internationale s'organise
france24fr.description: Deux séismes de magnitude 7 ont frappé le Venezuela, provoquant une situation « critique » selon les autorités, avec de nombreux morts et blessés déjà extraits des décombres. Le bilan reste encore difficile à établir, tandis que les secouristes poursuivent leurs opérations dans des conditions très difficiles. Plusieurs pays, dont la France, ont proposé d’envoyer de l’aide humanitaire et des équipes de secours. Les précisions sur place d'Alice Campaignolle, correspondante de France 24 à Caracas.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les supporters marocains fêtent leur qualification en 16es
france24fr.description: Le Maroc s'est imposé 4-2 contre Haïti dans un match riche en rebondissements mercredi 24 juin. Des centaines de supporters marocains ont fêté leur victoire face à Haïti et leur qualification en 16e de finale de la Coupe du monde. Les Lions de l'Atlas ​n'ont toutefois pas ‌réussi à devancer le Brésil au classement du groupe C.

france24fr.title: Colombie : recruter sur TikTok, la nouvelle stratégie des groupes armés
france24fr.description: Émission spéciale - En Colombie, où le conflit armé s’est intensifié ces dernières années, les publications qui font la promotion des groupes armés se multiplient sur les réseaux sociaux, notamment TikTok. L’objectif : attirer de nouvelles recrues - en particulier des jeunes, parfois mineurs. La rédaction des Observateurs de France 24 a enquêté pour comprendre les rouages de cette nouvelle forme de recrutement.

france24fr.title: Premier sommet franco-italien depuis 2020 à Antibes
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron et Giorgia Meloni se retrouvent à Antibes pour le premier sommet franco-italien depuis 2020. Les deux pays, dirigés par des gouvernements de sensibilité politique différente, avaient signé un traité de coopération en 2021 mais n’avaient plus réellement relancé ce format bilatéral depuis. Cette rencontre doit permettre de remettre à plat les relations et d’ouvrir une série de discussions sur de nombreux dossiers dans les mois à venir, notamment la défense, l’énergie et les grands

france24fr.title: Canicule historique en France : le pays étouffe sous des températures inédites
france24fr.description: La France traverse une canicule exceptionnelle avec des températures dépassant les 40°C sur une grande partie du territoire depuis plusieurs jours. Musées, villes, touristes et agriculture sont fortement impactés, tandis que les autorités alertent sur la poursuite de cet épisode extrême ce week-end.

france24fr.title: TotalEnergies bientôt fixé dans le procès à fort enjeu sur son devoir de vigilance climatique
france24fr.description: TotalEnergies attend la décision de justice dans le cadre du procès portant sur son devoir de vigilance. Cette affaire, très suivie, pourrait faire jurisprudence sur la responsabilité des grandes entreprises en matière d’impact environnemental et social de leurs activités. Les précisions de Marie Schuster depuis le tribunal de Paris.

france24fr.title: Au Gabon, les partis politiques sommés de se mettre en conformité
france24fr.description: Au Gabon, le gouvernement lance un ultimatum aux partis politiques. Les autorités demandent aux 104 formations recensées de se conformer aux nouvelles exigences administratives et légales sous peine de sanctions. Une démarche que certains opposants considèrent déjà comme une atteinte au pluralisme démocratique.

france24fr.title: Marco Rubio en tournée dans le Golfe pour rassurer les alliés des États-Unis
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire d’État américain Marco Rubio effectue une tournée au Koweït et dans plusieurs pays du Golfe, la première depuis l’accord avec l’Iran. Washington cherche à rassurer ses partenaires sur son engagement sécuritaire dans la région et à clarifier sa position face à Téhéran.

france24fr.title: France : des records de températures battus chaque jour, le gouvernement en alerte
france24fr.description: La France fait face à une canicule avec des températures inédites, poussant le gouvernement à activer la phase 3 du plan Orsan. Sébastien Lecornu annonce un basculement vers l’action, avec une réorganisation des effectifs hospitaliers pour faire face à la crise, ainsi qu’un renforcement de la coopération entre hôpitaux et médecine de ville. Les précisions de Clovis Casali.

france24fr.title: Entre Hollywood et la Palestine, le combat d'Hiam Abbass
france24fr.description: De Nazareth à Hollywood, Hiam Abbass a construit une carrière rare, entre grandes productions internationales et cinéma d'auteur engagé. Connue du grand public pour ses rôles dans la série "Succession", les films de Steven Spielberg, Jim Jarmusch ou encore Denis Villeneuve, l'actrice et réalisatrice franco-palestinienne n'a jamais cessé de faire entendre une voix singulière.

nzz.description: Frankreich erlebt eine historische Hitzewelle. Marine Le Pen verspricht, das Land mit Klimaanlagen zu überziehen, sollte sie 2027 zur Präsidentin gewählt werden. Das halten ihre Gegner für Populismus.

nzz.description: Die UBS hofft, dass ihr das Parlament entgegenkommt bei den neuen Eigenkapitalregeln. Ihr Gegenspieler, der Bundesrat, erhält nun aber Unterstützung von der wichtigsten multilateralen Finanzorganisation.

nzz.description: In Frankreich wurde am Dienstag der heisseste Tag seit Beginn der Wetteraufzeichnungen registriert. Der Spitzenwert von 44,3 Grad Celsius wurde in der Gemeinde Pissos gemessen. Die Hitzewelle in Europa soll bis zum Wochenende andauern.

nzz.title: Als Teilchenphysiker hat Günther Dissertori 5000 Forscher koordiniert. Jetzt wird er Präsident der ETH Zürich mit 13 000 Angestellten
nzz.description: Die Entdeckung des Higgs-Teilchens war der Höhepunkt seiner Karriere. Jetzt will er die renommierte Hochschule in die Zukunft führen.

nzz.title: Volkswagen verschafft sich mit einem Verkauf Luft für den grossen Umbau
nzz.description: Der Autobauer gibt die Mehrheit an seinem Tochterunternehmen Everllence an den Finanzinvestor Bain ab. Damit bekommen auch rund 900 Mitarbeiter in Zürich einen neuen Eigentümer.

nzz.title: An der WM sind 65 «Franzosen» dabei – ein Viertel der Teilnehmer laufen nicht für das Land auf, in dem sie geboren worden sind
nzz.description: Immer mehr Fussballer besitzen mehrere Staatsangehörigkeiten. Für kleinere Nationen ist die Suche nach Talenten im Ausland die einzige Chance für einen Platz auf der Weltbühne.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Karikatur der Woche
nzz.description: Der Karikaturist Peter Gut kommentiert in seinen wöchentlichen Zeichnungen für die NZZ das Weltgeschehen.

nzz.title: Eine «Erdbebendoublette»: Darum bebte die Erde in Venezuela so heftig

spiegel.title: Brandanschlag in Solingen 1993: Verurteilter beantragt nach 33 Jahren Wiederaufnahme
spiegel.description: Mehr als drei Jahrzehnte nach dem Brandanschlag, bei dem fünf türkeistämmige und türkische Frauen und Mädchen starben, beteuert einer der wegen Mordes Verurteilten seine Unschuld. Sein Anwalt will »neue Beweise« präsentieren.

spiegel.title: Hitze in Deutschland: So werden warme Räume wieder kühl (Kopie)
spiegel.description: 38 Grad im Juni – wie schaffen Sie es, dass die Gluthitze draußen bleibt? Ein Experte ordnet Alltagstipps und professionelle Installationen ein: von improvisierter Alufolie am Fenster bis zur ausgewachsenen Klimaanlage.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Erdbeben in Venezuela, AfD-Verbot, Fußball-WM
spiegel.description: Die AfD ist laut einem neuen Rechtsgutachten verfassungswidrig. Ein Doppel-Erdbeben erschüttert Venezuela. Und der weibliche Überraschungsstar dieser WM leitet heute Abend das deutsche Spiel gegen Ecuador. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: Erdbeben in Venezuela: »Die kommenden 48 Stunden werden entscheidend sein«
spiegel.description: Ein schweres Erdbeben hat Venezuela getroffen. Die Politologin Sabine Kurtenbach erklärt, wie nun auch der marode Zustand des Landes in den Blick rückt – und seine politische Führung.

spiegel.title: Bafög: Friedrich Merz stellt baldige Einigung auf Reform in Aussicht
spiegel.description: Monatelang rang die Koalition um die geplante Bafög-Reform, jetzt verspricht Friedrich Merz eine baldige Lösung. Der Kanzler müsse nun sein Wort halten und den »Zick-Zack-Kurs« beenden, drängt das Deutsche Studierendenwerk.

spiegel.title: Lionel Richie bricht Auftritt aus gesundheitlichen Gründen ab
spiegel.description: So hatten sich seine Fans den Tourauftakt sicher nicht vorgestellt: Lionel Richie hat ein Konzert nach einer knappen Stunde abbrechen müssen. Ihm sei schwindelig, erklärte der Soulstar.

spiegel.title: Apple erhöht Preise: Das neue MacBook hätten Sie lieber gestern kaufen sollen
spiegel.description: Es ist ein bisher einmaliger Vorgang: Preiserhöhungen bei Apple. Mac-Computer und iPads werden teurer. Die Schuld wird dem KI-Hype zugeschoben.

spiegel.title: Sudan – Obeid: Hunderttausende Menschen bereiten sich auf neue Eskalation vor
spiegel.description: Die RSF-Miliz hat mit nahezu täglichen Angriffen die Infrastruktur von Obeid weitgehend zerstört. Jetzt droht eine Offensive auf die sudanesische Stadt. Die Uno ist alarmiert.

spiegel.title: Clueso: »Ich habe kein Problem damit, Fuck AfD zu sagen«
spiegel.description: »Berühmtheit ist eine Währung«, sagt Clueso, einer der populärsten deutschen Musiker. Und politisch so engagiert wie nur wenige. Beim Hurricane-Festival spricht er über Haltung – und verrät, wie sein neuer Song klingt.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Ermittlerin im Block-Prozess hält Aussagen der Kinder für glaubhaft
spiegel.description: Im Entführungsfall um die Kinder von Christina Block befragen die Verteidiger die Hauptermittlerin. Sie wollen wissen: Könnte der Vater die Aussagen der Kinder beeinflusst haben?

spiegel.title: Deutschlands Straßen im Hitzestress: Wenn der Beton platzt und Asphalt aufweicht
spiegel.description: Steigende Temperaturen setzen Deutschlands Straßen einem Stresstest aus. Straßenbauer haben Ideen für hitzebeständigere Fahrbahnen.

spiegel.title: Bayer gewinnt Glyphosat-Streit in den USA vor Supreme Court
spiegel.description: Sieg für den Bayer-Konzern im milliardenschweren Rechtsstreit über mutmaßliche Krebsrisiken seines Unkrautvernichters Glyphosat: Das Oberste US-Gericht hat Tausenden Klagen wegen angeblich unzureichender Warnhinweise die Grundlage entzogen.

spiegel.title: Kapitalrente: Wie der Atomfonds Kenfo die deutsche Altersvorsorge verwalten soll
spiegel.description: Die Rentenkommission empfiehlt für Deutschland eine Kapitalrente nach schwedischem Vorbild. Verwalten könnte sie der Atomfonds Kenfo. Dessen Chefin Anja Mikus spricht von einer großen Chance für Millionen Menschen.

spiegel.title: Nutella-Rückruf: Muffins wegen möglicher Metallteile zurückgerufen
spiegel.description: Nutella-Fans aufgepasst: Ferrero zieht eine Charge Muffins aus dem Verkauf. Es besteht die Gefahr, dass diese mit Metallteilen verunreinigt wurden.

spiegel.title: Franz Hengsbach – Essen: Neue Missbrauchsvorwürfe gegen verstorbenen Kardinal
spiegel.description: Eine Studie listet weitere Missbrauchsvorwürfe gegen den früheren Essener Bischof Hengsbach auf. In mindestens vier Fällen halten die Forscher die Schilderungen für plausibel.

spiegel.title: Hitze News: Im Pariser Umland mangelt es mehreren Orten an Trinkwasser
spiegel.description: Neun Dörfer rund um Paris müssen mit Wasser aus Plastikflaschen versorgt werden. Im Süden und Osten Deutschland herrscht Dürre. Und: Feuer auf ehemaligem Panzerschießplatz. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Marine stoppt Tanker aus Russland – Emmanuel Macron postet Video von Zugriff
spiegel.description: Mithilfe von Frachtschiffen mit undurchsichtigen Eigentümerverhältnissen versucht Russland, Sanktionen zu umgehen. Frankreich reagiert robust: Ein von Präsident Macron verbreitetes Video zeigt Details eines Militäreinsatzes.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Deutschland ist nicht in Wechselstimmung
spiegel.description: Die Partie gegen Ecuador ist auf den ersten Blick sportlich irrelevant, Deutschland ist bereits Gruppensieger. Für das Team hat das Spiel dennoch seine Bedeutung. Alles Wichtige zum Duell mit den Südamerikanern.

observador.title: "Quando eu disse para fugir, foi quando o prédio caiu"
observador.description: Edifício de dois andares ruiu no centro do Porto. Lojista alertou trabalhadores de obras em terreno contíguo quando reparou em fissuras fora do normal. Escaparam "por segundos" ao colapso.

observador.title: Fundo soberano. Governo recusa "intervencionismo económico"
observador.description: O Governo continua sem abrir o jogo sobre o fundo soberano. Leitão Amaro agora fala em três setores -- banca, energia e seguros -- para defender soberania e segurança nacional.

observador.title: Pedro Neto pronto a "explodir" depois de lesões no passado
observador.description: Jogador do Chelsea não conseguiu ir ao Mundial do Qatar devido a lesões. Quer agora aproveitar a oportunidade neste campeonato do mundo, onde já foi titular nos dois primeiros jogos.

observador.title: EUA: pedidos de desemprego recuam para 215.000
observador.description: Menos 12.000 pedidos de subsídio de desemprego nos EUA face à semana anterior. Números da semana passada apontam 215.000 pedidos, segundo o Departamento do Trabalho norte-americano.

observador.title: Mulher de Bolsonaro rompe com candidatura de enteado
observador.description: A ex-primeira-dama acusa o enteado de a ter tratado com desrespeito e afirma que a sua prioridade agora é cuidar de Jair Bolsonaro, em prisão domiciliária.

observador.title: Kristin. Derrocadas na EN2 continuam a preocupar Sardoal
observador.description: A circulação da EN2 continua encerrada em certas zonas devido ao risco associado. Reparação poderá ultrapassar os quatro milhões de euros e o município recebeu até hoje cerca de 540 mil euros.

observador.title: Kristin: Miranda do Corvo quer repor telecomunicações
observador.description: A moção exige "ao Governo a adoção de medidas urgentes que garantam a reposição integral dos serviços de telecomunicações ainda afetados e a normalização das condições de acesso das populações".

observador.title: Lula afirma que relação com Colômbia "transcende ideologias"
observador.description: O líder da esquerda brasileira reconheceu a vitória do candidato da extrema-direita um dia após o Conselho Nacional Eleitoral colombiano confirmar o resultado.

observador.title: 16h. Sismos. Cidadão Português entre as vítimas mortais
observador.description: O ministério dos negócios estrangeiros revela que há um português entre as vítimas mortais dos terramotos na Venezuela. Ainda neste jornal, a história de um lusodescendente que deu conta do sismo.

observador.title: Mais carros elétricos novos fazem baixar emissões médias
observador.description: A redução, explica a AEA, está ligada ao aumento da quota de veículos registados com emissões zero. Os dados baseiam-se em informações sobre todos os automóveis e carrinhas recém-registados.

observador.title: Apple aumenta preços devido à crise das memórias
observador.description: Tim Cook já tinha admitido que a Apple não estava a conseguir suportar a subida dos preços das memórias. Esta quinta-feira chegaram os aumentos, fruto de um "desafio sem precedentes" na indústria.

observador.title: "Patrocínio": uma lição riquíssima de "reality TV"
observador.description: A narrativa, os conflitos, as heroínas, as vilãs, as relações, os tabus e uma produção com dinheiro para comprar tempo: os seis episódios na Prime Video são obrigatórios, escreve Susana Verde.

observador.title: Vamos ficar de Olhos Abertos para a violência?
observador.description: A iniciativa da Comissão Europeia quer alertar para as diferentes formas de violência, utilizando os eventos Olhos Abertos para sensibilizar a população. Participe no desafio e faça parte desta causa.

observador.title: 15h. Sismos. Provável haver vítimas mortais portuguesas
observador.description: Paulo Rangel adianta que é provável haver portugueses entre as vítimas mortais dos terramotos. Ainda neste jornal, as atualizações sobre o estado das ruas venezuelanas.

observador.title: Fundo soberano na EDP? "Todos os acionistas são bem-vindos"
observador.description: A EDP faz 50 anos. Ao longo da vida passou de 100% pública para ser 100% privada. Sem querer comentar o fundo soberano. Miguel Stiwell dá as boas-vindas a todos os acionistas.

observador.title: Fuga de cloro gás em ETA em Aljustrel faz um ferido ligeiro
observador.description: Acidente ocorreu durante trabalhos de manutenção na ETA da barragem do Roxo. Trabalhador transportado para o hospital de Beja por precaução. Fuga já controlada.

observador.title: UE: acompanhantes de pessoas com deficiência têm voo grátis
observador.description: O eurodeputado Matteo Ricci, que redigiu a proposta do Parlamento Europeu, afirma que, com a aprovação desta medida, chegam agora outras "mais robustas" para ajudar pessoas com mobilidade reduzida.

observador.title: Um tomate tem mais tecnologia do que um Ferrari?
observador.description: Luís Mira, da CAP, revela o lado tecnológico do mundo rural: de sensores de rega a microrganismos que regeneram o solo.

phys-org.title: Heat-struck Italians cool off in ancient stone 'trulli'
phys-org.description: Once relics of a bygone way of life, the iconic dry-stone dwellings with conical roofs dotted across Puglia are in increasing demand as cool havens in Italy's sweltering south.

phys-org.title: Hybrid reef project off Miami Beach targets wave attenuation and coral recovery
phys-org.description: University of Miami researchers and collaborators have expanded an offshore reef restoration and coastal resilience project off Miami Beach with the deployment of three 3D-printed SEAHIVE clustered structures.

phys-org.title: Sponges may cut methylmercury contamination in marine food webs by more than 50%
phys-org.description: Marine sponges may play an important, previously underestimated role in reducing methylmercury contamination in marine food webs. In a new modeling study, researchers at Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon showed that sponges can significantly influence the spread of this environmental toxin through ecosystems. The findings suggest that the animals' unique feeding behavior helps reduce methylmercury levels and may lower contamination in fish. The study is published in the journal Biogeosciences.

phys-org.title: Heat wave bakes 100 mn Europeans at over 35C
phys-org.description: At least 101 million Europeans were forecast to swelter in temperatures of more than 35C on Thursday, as scores of people were thought to have been killed by the heat wave.

phys-org.title: Study explores environmental cost, perceptions of influencer PR gifts
phys-org.description: As part of their marketing strategy, many companies send public relations packages full of curated products to social media influencers, who film themselves opening the gifts on platforms like Instagram and TikTok.

phys-org.title: Turtles may migrate using Earth's magnetic field
phys-org.description: New research indicates that sea turtles seem to navigate across hundreds of miles of open ocean using Earth's magnetic field. Previous experimental studies suggested that sea turtles use geomagnetism to navigate, but this study, published in Science Advances, was purely observational: Researchers attached devices measuring location and compass direction (the way a turtle was facing at a given moment) to six female green sea turtles that took about a month to navigate more than 1,000 miles (

phys-org.title: Taking a step back changes group discussions in virtual environments
phys-org.description: In group decision-making, it is critical for each member to engage in discussions with a broader perspective and without fixating on personal values and knowledge. While self-distancing, or stepping back and viewing oneself from a third-person perspective, has been associated with more objective thinking, its role in multiparty decision-making within virtual environments remains underexplored.

phys-org.title: Apes and humans have been sharing a laugh for 15 million years
phys-org.description: Great apes may have been laughing with a similar rhythm to modern humans for at least 15 million years, a University of Warwick study reveals. The finding offers unexpected clues to how human speech evolved.

phys-org.title: Trios of quantum particles form checkerboard layouts when particle density hits sweet spot
phys-org.description: Trions form when three particles, like quarks or electrons, come together. This formation occurs in quantum particles in nuclear physics, semiconductors and magnets, and understanding its behavior can be challenging. Rice University's Kaden Hazzard and his team recently developed a theory on how these formations occur and behave, which was published in Physical Review Letters.

phys-org.title: Researchers identify dual-function rice gene that boosts drought tolerance and grain yield
phys-org.description: As climate change intensifies droughts and other environmental stresses, maintaining crop productivity has become a major challenge for global agriculture. Drought can impair chloroplast development, reducing photosynthetic efficiency and ultimately lowering crop yields.

phys-org.title: What really controls water chemistry in nanoscale spaces
phys-org.description: Water is the most studied molecule on Earth, yet a surprisingly basic question has gone unanswered for decades: When water is squeezed into gaps just a few molecules wide—as happens inside nanoscale pores, membranes and biological channels—does it become more or less chemically reactive?

phys-org.title: Study analyzes how genes and education influence socioeconomic success
phys-org.description: Ambitious public education policies have the capacity to cushion the role of the "genetic lottery" in people's life chances. This is one of the main conclusions of a scientific study by Universidad Carlos III de Madrid (UC3M), the University of Lausanne (Switzerland) and Stockholm University (Sweden) analyzing the impact of an educational reform in England. These findings could be applied to the design of future educational policies.

phys-org.title: Thirsty desert lizards inspire a new water-harvesting system
phys-org.description: When the desert horned lizard (Phrynosoma platyrhinos) is thirsty, it cannot just lap up water or scoop it up like a bird because it lives in environments where water is extremely scarce. Typically, it's found in damp soil or, even more rarely, in drops of rain.

phys-org.title: Megacluster of bacterial genes reveals four antibiotics that jointly starve rivals of biotin
phys-org.description: Researchers at McMaster University have discovered what they describe as a "megacluster" of genes in Streptomyces bacteria that produces four antibiotics that work together to stop rival bacteria.

phys-org.title: Semi-communal 'compound houses' in Ghana affect how people participate in political activity
phys-org.description: Could the precise architectural form of your residence influence how much you participate in politics? A new study by MIT scholars finds this to be exactly the case—at least in Accra, Ghana, where many people live in semi-communal structures known as "compound houses," often sharing kitchens, bathrooms and common living-room spaces, while having private bedrooms.

phys-org.title: Researchers develop a new prodrug and localized drug delivery platform for selective treatment of cancer
phys-org.description: A new collaborative study reports the discovery and application of a novel therapeutic strategy to selectively target EGFR and other kinases with controlled release in tumor microenvironments to improve therapeutic efficacy, with promising results. The research is published in Bioorganic Chemistry.

phys-org.title: This single well-known and widespread butterfly is actually three species in disguise
phys-org.description: The tropical rainforests of Central and South America are among the most biodiverse places on Earth. Costa Rica alone is home to half a million species, five times more than exist in the entire country of Canada, despite the former having 200 times less land area than the latter.

phys-org.title: Tiny water droplets transmutate aniline into pyridine in ambient and catalyst-free conditions
phys-org.description: Aniline can now be transformed into pyridine without adding any catalysts, oxidants or toxic reagents. In a recent study published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, researchers achieved skeletal editing, involving the reorganization of the carbon-nitrogen bonds within an aromatic ring, by turning an aqueous solution of aniline into a mist of microdroplets.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.
